## Company Overview

Lanos Logic is an AI automation company based in Chicago, Illinois and the United Kingdom, serving clients across the US, UK, and internationally. We build AI agents, voice AI agents, document automation, process automation, vector database (RAG) retrieval, mobile applications, and analytics platforms. Engagements start with a free discovery call and a BPMN process map, are quoted at a fixed price before any build, and typically deliver in 2-6 weeks.

We work across marketing and sales agencies, e-commerce, healthcare, real estate, logistics, education, professional services, manufacturing, government and public sector, pharmaceutical, life sciences, financial services, law firms and attorneys, and immigration law practices. The deepest proof is in document-heavy regulated work: legal contract and case automation, education enrolment, and healthcare certification.

## Services

### Vector Database Solutions

Vector database solutions store your documents as numerical embeddings so AI can search by meaning instead of exact keywords. Lanos Logic builds enterprise-grade vector database architecture for semantic search, knowledge retrieval, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) across massive document collections.

A vector database stores your documents, tickets, contracts, and knowledge as high-dimensional embeddings — numerical fingerprints of meaning — so an AI can retrieve information by intent rather than exact keywords. When someone asks "which suppliers can ship refrigerated freight to Texas," a keyword search needs those literal words to appear; a vector search finds the right passage even when the document says "cold-chain logistics, Dallas hub." Lanos Logic designs and builds this retrieval layer end to end: chunking and cleaning your source content, generating embeddings, indexing them in a production vector store, and tuning similarity search for precision and recall on your real queries.

Most clients use a vector database as the foundation for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), where an AI assistant answers from your proprietary data instead of guessing. We build the full pipeline — document ingestion, embedding models, the vector index, and a retrieval step that grounds every AI response in cited source passages — so answers stay accurate and auditable. The same architecture powers internal knowledge search, customer-facing support bots, and contract or policy lookup across collections that scale from a few thousand documents to billions of embeddings.

A typical engagement starts with a free discovery call and a BPMN analysis of where your team loses time hunting for information, then a fixed-price build delivered in 2-6 weeks. Because retrieval is grounded and source-cited, teams find the right document in seconds instead of minutes and trust the answers enough to act on them. Vector Database Solutions pair naturally with our AI Agents and Document Automation services when you want the retrieved knowledge to drive a conversation or trigger a workflow.

**Features:**
- Semantic Search & Retrieval
- Document Embedding Pipelines
- RAG Architecture Design

**Benefits:**
- **Instant Knowledge Discovery** — Find relevant information across millions of documents in seconds using semantic similarity.
- **Enterprise RAG Systems** — Build retrieval-augmented generation systems that ground AI responses in your proprietary data.
- **Scalable Architecture** — Vector database infrastructure that scales from thousands to billions of embeddings.

**Frequently Asked Questions:**

Q: What is a vector database and why do I need one?
A: A vector database stores the meaning of your content as embeddings so you can run semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). It lets AI answer questions grounded in your proprietary documents instead of guessing.

Q: What is RAG (retrieval-augmented generation)?
A: RAG combines a vector database with a language model: relevant passages are retrieved from your data and given to the model so its answers are accurate, current, and traceable to your sources.

Q: How large a document collection can a vector database handle?
A: Our architectures scale from thousands to billions of embeddings. One client unified 15+ years of research into semantic search across 2M+ documents, cutting discovery time from weeks to minutes.

Q: How much does a vector database solution cost?
A: Cost depends on data volume, ingestion pipelines, and hosting. We scope it on a free discovery call and quote a fixed project price for the architecture and implementation.

URL: https://lanos-logic.com/services/vector-database-solutions

### AI Agents

AI agents are software assistants that understand natural language to automate customer interactions, answer queries, and complete multi-step tasks 24/7. Lanos Logic builds AI agents that work around the clock and scale with demand without increasing headcount.

An AI agent is a software assistant that understands natural language and completes real work — answering customer questions, qualifying leads, looking up account details, and carrying out multi-step tasks — 24/7 without a human in the loop for routine cases. Unlike a scripted chatbot, an agent holds context across a conversation, reasons about what the user actually needs, and calls your systems to get things done. Lanos Logic builds AI agents on Claude AI and connects them to your stack through Make.com, n8n, AirTable, and GoHighLevel so they can read and write the same data your team uses.

We design each agent around the jobs it must do: a support agent that resolves tier-1 tickets and escalates the rest, a sales agent that qualifies inbound leads and books meetings, or an operations agent that updates records and triggers downstream automations. The agent understands intent, pulls grounded answers from your knowledge base (often backed by our Vector Database Solutions), and performs actions through secured integrations — then hands off cleanly to a person whenever a request falls outside its scope, with full conversation context attached.

The result is capacity that scales with demand instead of headcount: one voice deployment qualifies 100-150 leads a week at a 98% completion rate, an email-processing agent handles 120+ messages a month and returns 38 hours, and a content agent cut creation time by 95% while lifting engagement 60%. Every agent is custom-scoped on a free discovery call, quoted as a fixed project price, and typically live within 2-6 weeks including testing against your real conversations. We monitor and tune the agent after launch so accuracy improves as it sees more traffic.

**Features:**
- Natural Language Processing
- Contextual Understanding
- Multi-task Automation

**Benefits:**
- **24/7 Availability** — Provide round-the-clock service without increasing staffing costs.
- **Reduced Response Time** — Instant responses to customer inquiries, improving satisfaction.
- **Scalability** — Handle increasing volumes of interactions without proportional cost increases.

**Frequently Asked Questions:**

Q: What is an AI agent and what can it do?
A: An AI agent is an intelligent virtual assistant that automates customer interactions, answers queries using natural language, and executes multi-step tasks 24/7 with contextual understanding of your business.

Q: How much does an AI agent cost?
A: AI agents are custom-built and priced per project after a free discovery call. Cost depends on the channels covered, the integrations required, and the complexity of the tasks the agent automates.

Q: Will an AI agent replace my support team?
A: No — it augments them. AI agents handle high-volume, repetitive queries instantly so your team can focus on complex, high-value conversations, with smooth hand-off when human judgement is needed.

Q: How long does it take to deploy an AI agent?
A: Most AI agents are deployed within 2-6 weeks, following our Analyze, Prepare, and Implement process and grounded in your real knowledge base and workflows.

### Voice AI Agents

Voice AI agents are automated phone assistants that answer and place calls, qualify leads, book appointments, and handle customer support 24/7 with natural, human-like conversation. Lanos Logic builds voice AI agents that capture every call and hand off to a human team member when needed.

A voice AI agent is an automated phone assistant that answers and places calls with natural, human-like conversation — qualifying leads, booking appointments, taking orders, and handling support around the clock. Lanos Logic builds voice agents on VAPI and Twilio telephony, integrated with your calendar, CRM, and automations, so the agent does more than talk: it checks availability, writes the booking, updates the contact record, and sends the confirmation. Callers get answered on the first ring at any hour instead of reaching voicemail.

We design the call flow around your business — the intents the agent should handle, the questions it asks to qualify a caller, and the exact point where it performs a warm hand-off to a human team member. The agent recognizes when a conversation needs a person (a complex complaint, a high-value deal, a request outside its scope) and transfers with full context so the caller never repeats themselves. Because it runs on real telephony, it works for inbound reception, outbound follow-up campaigns, appointment reminders, and after-hours coverage.

For most clients the highest ROI is simply capturing calls that used to be missed — every after-hours or overflow call that would have gone to voicemail becomes a booked appointment or a qualified lead. A focused voice deployment is typically live within 2-4 weeks, including script design, telephony integration, and tuning against real call recordings, and is quoted as a fixed project price after a free discovery call. Voice AI Agents pair with our Communication Automation service when you want SMS follow-up to fire automatically after a call.

Q: Can the voice agent transfer calls to a human?
A: Yes. Our voice agents handle the conversation autonomously and perform a seamless warm hand-off to a human team member whenever a call needs escalation or a request falls outside their scope.

Q: How long does it take to launch a voice AI agent?

### Document Automation

Document automation uses AI to read documents, extract data, manage contracts, and run approval workflows automatically, turning hours of manual paperwork into minutes. Lanos Logic builds document automation with OCR, data extraction, e-signature, and compliance-ready audit trails.

Document automation turns hours of manual paperwork into minutes by letting AI read documents, extract the data that matters, route them for approval, and file them with a clean audit trail. Lanos Logic builds the full pipeline: OCR and AI-powered data extraction that pulls fields from PDFs, scans, and forms; contract generation and e-signature through DocuSign or PandaDoc; and approval workflows orchestrated in Make.com or n8n that move a document from intake to signed to archived without anyone rekeying information.

A common build looks like this: a contract or application arrives by email, the system extracts the customer details and key terms, validates them against your records in AirTable or your CRM, generates the right document from a template, sends it for signature, and — once signed — updates every connected system and stores a compliance-ready copy. Because extraction is AI-driven rather than template-rigid, it handles the messy variety of real-world documents while keeping accuracy high and eliminating the transcription errors that creep into manual data entry.

Clients in legal, healthcare, finance, and care services use this to collapse onboarding and contract cycles — commonly cutting document processing time by up to 90% — while maintaining the audit trails that PCI-DSS, SOC 2, HIPAA, and internal compliance require. Every workflow is mapped on a free discovery call with a BPMN analysis, quoted at a fixed price, and typically delivered in 2-6 weeks. Document Automation pairs with our Vector Database Solutions when you also need to search the contents of everything you process.

**Features:**
- OCR & Data Extraction
- Contract Management
- Approval Workflows

**Benefits:**
- **Reduce Processing Time** — Automate document handling from hours to minutes.
- **Eliminate Errors** — AI-powered accuracy in data extraction.
- **Compliance Ready** — Maintain audit trails and compliance standards.

**Frequently Asked Questions:**

### Process Automation

Process automation connects your systems and software to run repetitive business workflows end to end without manual effort. Lanos Logic designs process automation that eliminates repetitive tasks, integrates your existing tools, and streamlines operations.

Process automation connects the systems you already use and runs your repetitive, multi-step workflows end to end — no copy-paste, no swivel-chair between tabs, no tasks forgotten on a Friday afternoon. Lanos Logic designs these workflows on Make.com, n8n, and Zapier, integrating tools like AirTable, GoHighLevel, ClickUp, Stripe, and Twilio so data flows automatically from one step to the next. We start by mapping your current process in BPMN with Miro, find the steps that are pure mechanical effort, and rebuild them as a reliable automation with error handling and alerts.

The work that disappears is the work nobody should be doing by hand: a new order in Stripe creating a project in ClickUp and a record in AirTable, a form submission triggering a sequence of emails and SMS, data syncing between two systems that were never meant to talk, or a nightly reconciliation that used to take an analyst an hour. Each automation is built to run unattended, retry on transient failures, and notify a human only when something genuinely needs judgment — so your team trades repetitive operations work for the exceptions that actually need them.

Because the automation enforces a single consistent path, it removes the human errors that come from manual handoffs and frees staff for higher-value work. Engagements are scoped on a free discovery call, quoted as a fixed project price, and typically delivered in 2-6 weeks following our Analyze, Prepare, Implement process. Process Automation is the connective tissue behind most of our other services — AI Agents, Document Automation, and Communication Automation all rely on it to actually move data and trigger actions.

### Communication Automation

Communication automation delivers SMS, voice, and multi-channel messaging to customers automatically and at scale. Lanos Logic builds Twilio-powered communication automation for fast, personalized, two-way customer messaging.

Communication automation delivers SMS, voice, and multi-channel messaging to your customers automatically and at scale — appointment reminders, order updates, payment links, re-engagement campaigns, and two-way conversations that actually get replies. Lanos Logic builds these flows on Twilio, integrated with your CRM and automations through Make.com and n8n, so messages are triggered by real events (a booking, a missed call, an abandoned cart) and personalized with the customer’s own details rather than blasted generically.

Because it is two-way, the system does more than send: a customer can reply to confirm, reschedule, or ask a question, and that response routes into your workflow or to a human — or to one of our AI Agents — for an instant answer. Voice broadcasting handles announcements and reminders at volume, while multi-channel logic falls back from one channel to another so an important message reaches the customer wherever they actually respond. Everything is logged against the contact record for a complete communication history.

Clients use this to lift response and conversion — personalized, well-timed messaging commonly drives meaningfully higher response rates and faster lead follow-up — while removing the manual effort of chasing customers one at a time. Each build is scoped on a free discovery call, quoted at a fixed project price, and typically live within 2-6 weeks. Clients commonly use these dashboards to justify expanding automation across more of the business once they can see the returns clearly. ### Agentic SEO & GEO

Agentic SEO and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) make your website the source AI assistants cite — optimizing for ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Gemini, not just classic search rankings. Lanos Logic structures your content, schema, and crawler access so large language models can find, understand, and quote your business by name.

Search is moving from a list of blue links to a single AI-generated answer. People increasingly ask ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews instead of scrolling a results page — and those assistants cite a handful of sources rather than ranking ten. Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), also called Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of making sure your business is one of the sources the AI quotes by name. Lanos Logic optimizes your site for how language models actually retrieve and cite content, so you show up where your buyers are now starting their research.

Our process starts with an audit of how AI systems see you today: which AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and others) can reach your site, what structured data you expose, and whether your content is even retrievable. We then make your pages machine-legible — adding JSON-LD schema (Organization, Service, FAQ, Speakable), an llms.txt and llms-full.txt knowledge base, and agent-native surfaces like an MCP endpoint and agent.json so assistants can read you directly. The core of the work is structuring content for hybrid retrieval: AI search engines fuse keyword (lexical) and meaning-based (semantic) search using Reciprocal Rank Fusion, so we co-locate clear question-and-answer passages, entity names, and self-contained explanations that score in both — the passages models actually pull into an answer.

Why it matters: if your competitors are the ones being cited in AI answers, you lose the buyer before they ever reach a search result or your homepage — and unlike a ranking you can watch, you never see it happen. GEO is also durable; the structured, well-explained content that earns citations keeps working as models update. Every engagement begins with a free discovery call and a visibility audit, is quoted as a fixed project price, and includes measurement of where AI engines mention your brand so we can close the gaps. Agentic SEO & GEO pairs naturally with our Vector Database Solutions and AI Agents work when you also want an assistant of your own grounded in the same content.

We deliver this through the 5-Layer GEO Stack — the same system we run on our own website: (1) Crawl Access — make sure AI crawlers like GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and OAI-SearchBot can reach and read your site; (2) Machine Legibility — JSON-LD schema, an llms.txt / llms-full.txt knowledge base, and agent-native surfaces (MCP, agent.json) so models parse you cleanly; (3) Retrieval-Ready Content — self-contained, question-and-answer passages tuned for the hybrid lexical and semantic retrieval (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) that AI engines use to pick sources; (4) Authority & Citations — the entity consistency, citations, and mentions that make a model trust and repeat your brand; and (5) Visibility Monitoring — tracking where and how you are cited across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini so we can close the gaps.

**Features:**
- Generative & Answer Engine Optimization
- llms.txt, Schema & AI Crawler Access
- Hybrid Retrieval (RRF) Content Structuring

**Benefits:**
- **Get Cited by AI Assistants** — Become the answer ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews surface when buyers research — where more of the journey now starts.
- **Future-Proof Visibility** — As search shifts from ten blue links to AI-generated answers, your content stays discoverable and quotable by the models that matter.
- **Measurable AI Presence** — See where and how AI engines mention your brand, then close the gaps that keep you out of generated answers.

**Frequently Asked Questions:**

Q: What is GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)?
A: GEO, also called Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of optimizing a website so AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews cite it in their generated answers. Instead of chasing classic keyword rankings, GEO makes your content easy for large language models to find, understand, and quote by name.

Q: How is GEO different from traditional SEO?
A: Traditional SEO optimizes for ranking on a page of blue links; GEO optimizes for being the source an AI quotes inside a single generated answer. The two overlap on fundamentals (crawlability, clear content, structured data) but GEO adds AI-crawler access, llms.txt knowledge bases, schema for machine reading, and content structured for the hybrid lexical+semantic retrieval AI engines use.

Q: Which AI search engines does Lanos Logic optimize for?
A: We optimize for the assistants and AI search surfaces buyers actually use: ChatGPT and ChatGPT Search, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Gemini, and Bing Copilot. We make sure their crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, OAI-SearchBot and others) can access your site and that your content is structured to be retrieved and cited.

Q: How do you get a website cited by ChatGPT or Perplexity?
A: We audit how AI systems see your site, open access to AI crawlers, add JSON-LD schema and an llms.txt/llms-full.txt knowledge base, and restructure content into self-contained, question-and-answer passages that score well in both keyword and semantic retrieval (the Reciprocal Rank Fusion that AI engines use to pick sources). We can also add agent-native surfaces like an MCP endpoint so assistants can read your business directly.

Q: How much does agentic SEO / GEO cost and how long does it take?
A: It is scoped on a free discovery call and quoted as a fixed project price based on the size of your site and the depth of optimization. An initial GEO audit and the core structural work are typically delivered within 2-6 weeks, with ongoing measurement of where AI engines mention your brand so we can keep closing gaps.

URL: https://lanos-logic.com/services/agentic-seo-geo

### Application Security Testing

Application security testing finds vulnerabilities in your code, dependencies, and build pipeline before they reach production. Lanos Logic sets up SAST, DAST, software composition analysis (SCA), secret scanning, and container and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) scanning inside your CI/CD as an always-on system: rules update themselves, AI triage cuts the noise, and developers see a short list of real issues on every pull request.

Application security testing (AST) finds vulnerabilities in the software you build before attackers find them in production. Lanos Logic builds it into your development workflow with five complementary techniques. Static application security testing (SAST) reads your source code for flaws such as injection, unsafe deserialisation, and broken authorisation logic. Dynamic application security testing (DAST) attacks the running application from the outside, the way an attacker would, and catches issues that only appear at runtime. Software composition analysis (SCA) inventories your open-source dependencies and flags known CVEs and licence risks. Secret scanning finds API keys, tokens, and passwords committed to code or buried in git history. Container and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) scanning checks Docker images, Kubernetes manifests, and Terraform or CloudFormation templates for vulnerable packages and insecure defaults before anything is deployed.

We wire these checks into the tools your team already uses - GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps - so results appear on the pull request instead of in a separate report nobody reads. We use proven open-source and commercial scanners, tune their rules to your languages and frameworks, triage the first baseline with you, and agree a gating policy so builds fail only on real, high-severity issues. Pre-commit secret checks stop credentials before they ever leave a laptop, and every build can produce a software bill of materials (SBOM) for customers and auditors.

This is not a one-off audit. Threats and dependencies change every day, so the system keeps itself current: scanning rules and vulnerability databases update automatically, an AI triage layer checks whether a vulnerable function is actually reachable from your code and ranks findings by real risk, and routine fixes such as dependency upgrades arrive as ready-to-review pull requests. Every flaw you fix becomes a permanent check, so the system flags it if the same mistake comes back. Our engineers stay in the loop to review AI decisions and tune what the system learns.

Application Security Testing is the shift-left layer of our cybersecurity practice: it finds what is wrong in the code. Security Vulnerability Scanning watches what is deployed, Penetration Testing proves what an attacker could actually do, and Systems Hardening & Cloud Posture closes the configuration gaps. Together they give evidence for the secure-development controls in SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS. The setup is scoped on a free discovery call and quoted at a fixed price, with optional ongoing triage support.

**Features:**
- SAST & DAST (Static and Dynamic Testing)
- SCA & Secret Scanning
- Container & Infrastructure-as-Code Scanning

**Benefits:**
- **Catch Issues Before Release** — Flaws are flagged on the pull request that introduces them, when a fix takes minutes instead of an emergency patch.
- **Supply-Chain Visibility** — Know every open-source package and container base image you ship, which ones carry known CVEs or licence risk, and produce an SBOM on demand.
- **AI Triage, Low Noise** — An AI layer checks whether a flaw is actually reachable, ranks it, and drafts the fix, so builds fail only on real, high-severity issues and developers keep trusting the alerts.

**Frequently Asked Questions:**

Q: What is the difference between SAST and DAST?
A: SAST (static application security testing) reads your source code without running it and points to the exact file and line of a flaw, such as an injection or a missing authorisation check. DAST (dynamic application security testing) attacks the running application from the outside and finds issues that only appear at runtime, such as misconfigured headers, session handling, or exposed endpoints. They catch different problems, so we run both.

Q: What are SCA and secret scanning?
A: Software composition analysis (SCA) lists every open-source library and package your application depends on, including indirect ones, and flags versions with known CVEs or risky licences. Secret scanning searches code, configuration, and git history for API keys, tokens, passwords, and private keys, and can block a commit before a secret leaves a developer’s machine.

Q: What do container and IaC scanning check?
A: Container scanning checks Docker images and their base layers for vulnerable OS packages and insecure settings such as running as root. Infrastructure-as-code (IaC) scanning checks Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes manifests, and Helm charts for misconfigurations - public buckets, open security groups, missing encryption - before they are deployed.

Q: Will security scanning slow down our developers?
A: It should not. Fast checks (secrets, SAST on changed files, SCA) run on each pull request in minutes; heavier DAST scans run nightly or against staging. We tune rules and triage the first baseline so builds fail only on real, high-severity issues instead of burying the team in noise.

Q: How much does application security testing cost and how do I get started?
A: It is scoped on a free discovery call based on your repositories, languages, and CI/CD platform, then quoted as a fixed price for the setup, with optional ongoing triage support. Most pipelines are scanning within one to three weeks.

Q: Is this a one-off audit?
A: No. We implement a system that keeps running and keeps itself current. Scanning rules and vulnerability databases update automatically, AI triage checks reachability and drafts fixes, and every fixed flaw becomes a permanent check. Threats change daily, so the protection has to as well.

URL: https://lanos-logic.com/services/application-security-testing

### Security Vulnerability Scanning

Security vulnerability scanning is the continuous, automated process of finding known weaknesses in everything you have deployed - websites, APIs, servers, containers, and cloud accounts - before attackers do. Lanos Logic scans your external attack surface and internal network against the OWASP Top 10 and daily-updated CVE databases, and runs it as a self-updating system: new assets join the scope automatically, new CVEs are matched to your inventory the day they are published, and AI ranks what to fix first.

Security vulnerability scanning is the continuous, automated process of finding known weaknesses in everything you have deployed - websites, APIs, servers, containers, and cloud accounts - before attackers do. Lanos Logic maps your external attack surface (domains, subdomains, open ports, exposed admin panels, expiring TLS certificates), scans internal networks and hosts, runs authenticated and unauthenticated web scans against the OWASP Top 10, and checks running container images and registries against daily-updated CVE databases. Scans run on a schedule and after meaningful changes, so newly disclosed CVEs and zero-days are caught as they emerge.

Every finding is validated to cut false positives, CVSS-scored, and mapped to business impact, so remediation effort goes to the issues that actually matter first. Reports say where the weakness is, why it is exploitable, and how to fix it, and alerts go to the channel your team already watches - email, Slack, Teams, or your ticketing system. Dated scan history doubles as evidence for PCI-DSS, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA audits.

The programme is a self-updating system, not a quarterly report. Asset discovery reruns automatically, so a new subdomain, server, or cloud service joins the scope without anyone filing a ticket. Each newly published CVE is matched against your inventory the same day, and an AI layer ranks it using real-world exploit signals such as the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue and EPSS scores together with how exposed the asset is. False positives you dismiss teach the system what to ignore next time.

Engagements are scoped on a free discovery call and quoted at a fixed price, and the programme is built to run continuously rather than as a one-off. Security Vulnerability Scanning is the detection layer for what is already live. It pairs with Application Security Testing, which catches flaws in code before release, Penetration Testing for adversarial validation, and Systems Hardening & Cloud Posture to fix the configuration weaknesses scanning surfaces.

**Features:**
- External Attack Surface & Network Scanning
- OWASP Top 10 & CVE Detection
- Self-Updating, AI-Prioritised Monitoring

**Benefits:**
- **Proactive Threat Detection** — Find and fix exposed services, outdated software, and newly disclosed CVEs before attackers exploit them.
- **Compliance Coverage** — Meet PCI-DSS, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA scanning requirements with documented, dated scan evidence.
- **Risk Prioritization** — CVSS-scored findings mapped to business impact so your team focuses on critical issues first.

**Frequently Asked Questions:**

Q: What is security vulnerability scanning?
A: Security vulnerability scanning is the continuous, automated process of finding known weaknesses in what you have deployed - websites, APIs, servers, containers, and cloud accounts - and checking them against the OWASP Top 10 and daily-updated CVE databases, so you can fix them before attackers exploit them.

Q: What is the difference between vulnerability scanning and application security testing?
A: Application security testing (SAST, SCA, secret and IaC scanning) looks inside your code and build pipeline before release. Vulnerability scanning looks at what is already live: your external attack surface, internal hosts, running containers, and cloud services. Most teams need both, because new CVEs are published every day for software that was clean when it shipped.

Q: How often should we run vulnerability scans?
A: External scans should run at least weekly and after every significant change; PCI-DSS requires quarterly external and internal scans as a minimum. We usually run continuous or daily external monitoring plus weekly authenticated scans, with alerts for newly disclosed critical CVEs that affect your stack.

Q: Is vulnerability scanning a substitute for a penetration test?
A: No. Scanning finds known weaknesses automatically and at scale; a penetration test uses a human attacker to prove which ones are exploitable and to find logic flaws scanners miss. Scanning keeps you covered between pentests.

Q: How much does vulnerability scanning cost?
A: It is scoped on a free discovery call based on the number of domains, IP addresses, applications, and cloud accounts in scope, and quoted as a fixed monthly or annual price.

Q: How does the scanning keep up with new threats?
A: It updates itself. New assets are discovered and added automatically, each newly published CVE is matched against your inventory the same day, and an AI layer ranks it using exploit signals such as the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue and EPSS together with your exposure. Dismissed false positives teach the system what to ignore.

URL: https://lanos-logic.com/services/security-vulnerability-scanning

### Penetration Testing

Penetration testing is an authorized, simulated cyberattack run by certified ethical hackers to expose exploitable vulnerabilities before real attackers find them. Lanos Logic pentests web apps, APIs, networks, and cloud infrastructure using PTES, OWASP, and MITRE ATT&CK methodologies, then keeps testing between engagements with automated attack simulation.

Penetration testing is an authorized, simulated cyberattack carried out by certified ethical hackers to expose exploitable vulnerabilities before real attackers find them. Lanos Logic pentests web applications, APIs, networks, and cloud infrastructure using industry-standard methodologies - PTES, the OWASP Web Security Testing Guide, and MITRE ATT&CK - so testing mirrors the tools, techniques, and procedures of actual adversaries rather than running a checklist. Where a scanner reports a potential issue, a pentester proves whether it can truly be exploited and how far an attacker could get.

Engagements can include web app and API testing against OWASP WSTG, network and cloud infrastructure testing, and social engineering or phishing simulations that test your people as well as your systems. Testing can be black-box (no prior knowledge, like an outside attacker), grey-box (a normal user account), or white-box (with source code and architecture access), and it targets what automated tools miss: business-logic flaws, chained low-severity issues, privilege escalation, and access-control gaps between tenants or roles.

A pentest is a snapshot, and attackers do not wait for the next one. Between manual engagements we run automated attack simulation that replays the techniques that worked against you, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, and adds new techniques as they are published. Every confirmed finding becomes an automated regression test, so you know if a fixed vulnerability reopens after a release, and the results tell our testers where to focus next time.

The reports are accepted as evidence for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, and regulatory audits, so a pentest satisfies both your security goals and your compliance obligations. Scope and timing are agreed on a free discovery call and quoted at a fixed price. Penetration Testing is the adversarial validation step in our cybersecurity practice, alongside Application Security Testing (flaws in code), Security Vulnerability Scanning (continuous detection), and Systems Hardening & Cloud Posture (closing the gaps testing reveals).

**Features:**
- Web App & API Pentesting (OWASP WSTG)
- Network & Cloud Infrastructure Testing
- Social Engineering & Phishing Simulations

**Benefits:**
- **Real-World Attack Simulation** — Test defenses under conditions that mirror actual attacker techniques, tools, and procedures (TTPs).
- **Detailed Remediation Roadmap** — Every finding includes reproduction steps, CVSS score, and step-by-step remediation guidance, and becomes an automated regression test that flags it if a fixed hole reopens.
- **Compliance Evidence** — Pentest reports accepted for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, and regulatory audits.

**Frequently Asked Questions:**

Q: What is penetration testing?
A: Penetration testing is an authorised, simulated cyberattack carried out by certified ethical hackers to find and prove exploitable vulnerabilities in your web apps, APIs, networks, and cloud infrastructure before real attackers do.

Q: What is the difference between black-box, grey-box, and white-box testing?
A: Black-box testing starts with no inside knowledge, like an external attacker. Grey-box testing starts with a normal user account, which is how most real breaches unfold. White-box testing includes source code and architecture access and gives the deepest coverage for the time spent. We recommend the approach on the scoping call based on your goals and compliance needs.

Q: How often should we run a penetration test?
A: At least once a year, and after major changes such as a new product, a large release, or a cloud migration. SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS auditors typically expect an annual test, and PCI-DSS also requires testing after significant changes.

Q: Will a penetration test disrupt our production systems?
A: Testing follows written rules of engagement that set scope, timing, and techniques. Destructive tests are excluded or run against staging, and we stop and call you immediately if we find a critical issue or anything unexpected.

Q: How long does a penetration test take and how much does it cost?
A: A focused web app or API test usually takes one to two weeks, with a report shortly after. Price depends on scope - applications, roles, endpoints, and network size - and is quoted as a fixed price after a free scoping call.

Q: What happens between penetration tests?
A: Automated attack simulation keeps running. It replays the techniques that worked against you, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, adds new techniques as they are published, and turns every confirmed finding into a regression test, so you know if a fixed vulnerability reopens after a release.

URL: https://lanos-logic.com/services/penetration-testing

### Systems Hardening & Cloud Posture

Systems hardening and cloud security posture management (CSPM) shrink your attack surface and keep it small. Lanos Logic configures servers, Kubernetes, and AWS, Azure, and GCP accounts against CIS Benchmarks, NIST SP 800-123, and Zero Trust principles, then keeps it that way with continuous, self-updating posture checks that catch drift and can fix safe issues automatically.

Systems hardening is the proactive work of configuring your servers, cloud infrastructure, and applications securely to shrink the attack surface an adversary can reach. Lanos Logic hardens systems with defense-in-depth controls following CIS Benchmarks, NIST SP 800-123, and Zero Trust Architecture principles - eliminating unnecessary services, closing exposed ports, enforcing least-privilege access, and tightening configurations across operating systems, databases, Kubernetes, and containers so there is simply less for an attacker to exploit.

Cloud security posture management (CSPM) keeps that hardened state from eroding. Misconfiguration is one of the most common causes of real-world cloud breaches, so we connect read-only posture checks to your AWS, Azure, and GCP accounts and continuously look for public storage buckets, over-permissive IAM roles and keys, security groups open to the internet, unencrypted data stores, and disabled audit logging. Each account gets a posture score against the CIS Foundations Benchmarks, and drift raises an alert the moment a change undoes a control.

Hardening is not done once and forgotten. Benchmark checks update automatically when CIS and cloud providers publish new guidance, drift is detected on every change, and an AI layer explains each deviation in plain language and proposes the fix. Safe, well-understood fixes, such as blocking public access on a storage bucket, can be applied automatically under approval rules you set; anything risky goes to an engineer.

The configurations are aligned with NIST, CIS, DISA STIG, and SOC 2 frameworks, so your environment is audit-ready and your security posture is documented rather than assumed. Changes are rolled out in stages with a rollback path to avoid disrupting production. Engagements are scoped on a free discovery call and quoted at a fixed price. Systems Hardening & Cloud Posture is the remediation-and-prevention layer of our cybersecurity practice, completing the loop with Application Security Testing, Vulnerability Scanning, and Penetration Testing.

**Features:**
- CIS Benchmark Implementation
- Cloud Security Posture Management (AWS, Azure, GCP)
- Zero Trust Architecture Design

**Benefits:**
- **Reduced Attack Surface** — Eliminate unnecessary services, close exposed ports, and enforce least-privilege access across your entire stack.
- **Regulatory Alignment** — Configurations aligned with NIST, CIS, DISA STIG, and SOC 2 frameworks for audit-ready security posture.
- **Continuous Cloud Posture** — Cloud accounts are checked continuously for public storage, over-permissive IAM, open security groups, and disabled logging, with drift alerts, automatic fixes for safe issues, and a posture score you can show auditors.

**Frequently Asked Questions:**

Q: What is systems hardening?
A: Systems hardening is the work of configuring servers, databases, containers, Kubernetes, and cloud accounts securely - removing unused services, closing ports, enforcing least privilege, and applying baselines such as the CIS Benchmarks - so attackers have far less to target.

Q: What is cloud security posture management (CSPM)?
A: CSPM continuously checks your AWS, Azure, and GCP accounts for risky configuration: public storage buckets, over-permissive IAM roles and keys, security groups open to the internet, unencrypted data, and disabled logging. It scores each account against benchmarks such as the CIS Foundations Benchmarks and alerts when a change undoes a control.

Q: Will hardening break our applications?
A: Staged rollout keeps that risk low. We assess current settings first, test changes in a non-production environment, roll them out gradually, and keep a rollback path for every change.

Q: Which standards do you harden against?
A: CIS Benchmarks and CIS Controls v8, NIST SP 800-123, DISA STIGs for regulated and government environments, NSA/CISA Kubernetes hardening guidance, and Zero Trust Architecture principles. The result is documented for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS audits.

Q: How much does systems hardening and cloud posture management cost?
A: It is scoped on a free discovery call based on the number of servers, clusters, and cloud accounts, then quoted as a fixed price for the hardening work, with optional ongoing posture monitoring.

Q: Can misconfigurations be fixed automatically?
A: Yes, within rules you set. Safe, well-understood fixes, such as blocking public access on a storage bucket or re-enabling audit logging, can be applied automatically and logged. Anything that could affect production goes to an engineer for approval, with an AI-written explanation of the risk and the proposed change.

URL: https://lanos-logic.com/services/systems-hardening

### White-Label Security for Agencies

White-label, continuous security testing for software agencies and development companies that build for their own clients. Lanos Logic runs automated weekly checks, our team verifies every finding, and we track each fix through to a retest. Your clients get verified findings, clear fix steps, and evidence that each issue was closed - not just another scan report.

White-Label Security for Agencies is a continuous security testing service for software agencies and development companies that build applications for their own clients. Instead of a one-off audit or a raw scanner export, you get a partner that runs automated weekly checks, has our team verify every finding, and tracks each fix through to a retest. Every report comes in an agency version and a clean version for your client, so the service fits the way you already deliver.

There are three packages. Monitor gives a consistent baseline: known vulnerabilities in dependencies and containers, exposed secrets, TLS and security headers, and new subdomains or open ports. Attack adds authenticated testing of your staging app every week and a monthly AI-assisted penetration test. Assure adds AI-assisted code review, proposed fix pull requests, a monthly call, quarterly compliance evidence, and an annual human penetration test through a partner firm. Pricing is per app per month and is quoted after a free scoping call.

Testing starts only with written authorization from the system owner. Attack testing runs on staging by default, and production receives non-destructive checks unless agreed otherwise. Results describe what was tested and when; they are not a guarantee that an app is secure. If your clients sell software or connected products in the EU, the Cyber Resilience Act matters now: since 11 September 2026, manufacturers in scope must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents. We provide early warning and evidence; the reporting duty stays with the manufacturer.

**Features:**
- Monitor, Attack, and Assure Packages
- Findings Verified by Our Team
- Fix Tracking Through to Retest

**Benefits:**
- **Delivered Under Your Brand** — Every report comes in an agency version for your team and a clean version you can hand to your client.
- **Verified, Not Just Scanned** — Each finding has evidence, business impact, and exact fix steps, prioritized by real exploitability rather than CVSS score alone.
- **Proof Each Issue Was Closed** — Findings become tickets in your client's Jira or GitHub, and we retest automatically before an issue is closed.

**Frequently Asked Questions:**

Q: What does white-label mean for this service?
A: We run the testing, verification, and retesting; you deliver the results to your client. Every report comes in two versions: an agency version with full technical detail for your team, and a clean version for the end client. Branding and terms are agreed when you sign up.

Q: Which package should we choose?
A: Monitor suits teams that need a consistent weekly baseline. Attack suits teams that ship often and need their login, access control, and APIs tested like an attacker would. Assure suits higher-risk apps or clients who ask for compliance evidence and an annual human penetration test.

Q: Do you test production systems?
A: Only with written authorization from the system owner. Attack testing runs on staging by default, and production receives non-destructive checks unless we agree otherwise in writing.

Q: How does the EU Cyber Resilience Act affect our clients?
A: Since 11 September 2026, manufacturers of products with digital elements that fall under the Cyber Resilience Act must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents. Not every client is in scope, so check with your client. Where it applies, we provide early warning and evidence; the reporting duty stays with the manufacturer.

Q: Does this mean the application is secure?
A: No testing service can promise that. Our findings and retests apply to what was tested and when. What you get is a consistent, verified view of risk, clear fix steps, and evidence of what has been closed.

Q: How is it priced?
A: Per app per month, by package. Pricing is quoted after a free scoping call based on the number of apps, environments, and the package you choose.

### Government & Public Sector

Document automation for government: Lanos Logic builds AI document processing, records automation, and case-management workflows for public sector teams, government contractors, and state and local agencies. We automate the intake, classification, generation, and e-signature of the forms and records that move through an agency — with full audit trails, role-based access, and data-residency control.

Document automation for government means taking the forms, applications, permits, licences, case files, and records that move through an agency and making them move without manual re-keying. Lanos Logic builds that pipeline end to end: AI-powered extraction that reads submitted PDFs, scans, and forms and pulls the fields that matter; validation against the systems of record you already run; automatic generation of the resulting letters, certificates, and determinations; e-signature through DocuSign or PandaDoc; and archival with a complete audit trail of who changed what and when. The orchestration layer is built on Make.com or n8n, so the workflow spans the tools a department already owns rather than requiring a platform migration.

The constraint that shapes public sector work is not technical difficulty, it is accountability. Every automated decision has to be explainable after the fact, every record has to be retrievable on request, and access has to be scoped so that staff see only what their role permits. We build to that from the start: role-based access control, immutable audit logging on every document touch, configurable data residency, and a human approval step wherever a determination affects a member of the public. Nothing is a black box — each automated step records its inputs, its output, and the rule it applied.

Our public sector delivery is a GPS lone-worker monitoring platform, built in 60 days, that keeps staff working alone in hazardous situations under 24/7 real-time location monitoring. The document automation described above is proven in the most document-heavy regulated environments we work in — a law firm that sends and tracks 10,000+ pre-filled contracts and reclaims 90 hours a month, and a pharmaceutical operation that cut prescription processing time by 90% in a seven-day build. If your procurement carries a specific authorization or accreditation requirement, raise it on the first call: we will tell you exactly what we hold and whether we are the right fit before anyone writes a proposal. ### Pharmaceutical

Pharma document automation: Lanos Logic automates the document-heavy operations around pharmaceutical work — prescription and order processing, submission and dossier assembly, SOP and label document generation, and content orchestration across the systems that hold them. We built a prescription automation flow that cut processing time by 90% and returned 47 hours a month. Vector-database retrieval makes the resulting document estate searchable by meaning, not filename.

Pharmaceutical operations run on documents — prescriptions and orders, batch and SOP records, label and artwork files, safety reports, and the submission packages assembled from all of them. Lanos Logic automates the handling of that estate: AI extraction that reads inbound documents and pulls structured data out of them, template-driven generation of the documents that go back out, routing and approval chains with sign-off recorded at each step, and synchronisation across the systems that hold the files, including SharePoint and internal APIs. The result is that a document arrives, is understood, triggers the right downstream actions, and lands in the right place with its approval history attached.

Content orchestration is the layer above that: keeping one approved version of a claim, a label, or a piece of clinical content consistent everywhere it appears, so a change approved once propagates rather than being re-typed into five systems. We build this with a vector database underneath, which indexes the document estate by meaning rather than filename. Someone can ask which documents cover a given indication, formulation, or market and get the right passages back with citations, even when none of those words appear literally in the file. That same retrieval layer is what grounds an AI assistant so its answers cite real source documents instead of improvising.

A US pharmaceutical client came to us with prescription processing that consumed most of a working week. We rebuilt it on AirTable, Make.com, PDF.co, and SharePoint with API integration into their existing stack: a 90% reduction in processing time, 47 hours returned every month, delivered in seven days. That engagement sat in commercial and prescriptions operations rather than R&D, and we are specific about the distinction for a reason — the extraction, assembly, approval-routing, and semantic retrieval patterns transfer directly to R&D document work, and we would rather show you the mechanism that produced a real result than claim a trial we have not run. Bring us the document workflow that is costing your team the most hours and we will map it on a free discovery call, quote a fixed price, and typically deliver in 2-6 weeks.

The mechanism is the same everywhere: the document is generated correctly the first time, its status is always visible, and nobody is maintaining a spreadsheet of who has signed.

Above the document layer sits retrieval. A vector database indexes your own precedent bank, executed agreements, and matter files by meaning, so an associate can ask for the clause or the prior matter that fits a situation and get the right passage back with a citation, rather than recalling which file it lived in. That retrieval layer also grounds any AI drafting assistance in your firm’s own work product instead of the open internet. ### Immigration Law

AI case management for immigration lawyers. Lanos Logic built a US immigration firm an AI-native platform covering 13 visa tracks — AI document intelligence that classifies and describes hundreds of exhibit documents, smart intake forms, drafting, USCIS PDF autofill, and a deadline engine with federal-holiday-aware H-1B premium processing countdowns. Built as a direct alternative to ManifestOS, Visalaw.ai, and Docketwise, and now running two offices.

Immigration law is document warfare. A single EB-5 petition can involve hundreds of source documents — bank statements, payslips, corporate records, affidavits — that must each be classified, described, ordered into an exhibit list, and woven into a source-of-funds narrative that survives USCIS scrutiny. An H-1B premium processing case lives or dies by a 15-business-day federal clock. Lanos Logic built a US immigration firm an AI-native case management platform for exactly this: AI document intelligence that classifies and describes every uploaded exhibit, smart intake forms that collect what each track actually requires, AI-assisted drafting, USCIS PDF autofill, and a deadline engine with federal-holiday-aware premium processing countdowns and automated alerts.

The platform covers 13 visa tracks and now runs two offices — the firm was founded in Washington and expanded by acquiring a Detroit practice, and both operate on the same system. It was built as a direct alternative to ManifestOS, Visalaw.ai, and Docketwise, because the firm wanted the case model to match how it actually works rather than bending its practice around a product roadmap it does not control. That is the real argument for building rather than buying in immigration: the software encodes your intake questions, your exhibit conventions, your deadline rules, and your quality bar, and it changes when your practice changes.

For immigration lawyers weighing this, the honest framing is that a platform build is a larger commitment than wiring up an off-the-shelf tool, and it pays back where volume and document complexity are high — petition-heavy practices, multi-office firms, and anyone whose associates are spending their days describing exhibits rather than arguing cases. We start with a free discovery call and a BPMN map of how a matter moves through your firm from consultation to filing, quote a fixed price before any build, and can scope it as a focused automation (intake, exhibit handling, or deadlines alone) rather than a full platform if that is the right first step.

## Case Studies

### US Immigration Law Firm - AI-Native Case Management Platform

- Industry: Finance & Legal · Vertical: Legal · Type: Code · Country: United States · Year: 2026
- Key results: 13 Visa tracks automated · 2 Offices unified · 300+ hrs Monthly hours saved

A US immigration law firm — founded in Washington and expanded through the acquisition of a Detroit practice — now runs both offices on a custom AI-native case management platform built by Lanos Logic: a serious contender to ManifestOS, Visalaw.ai, and Docketwise, covering 13 visa tracks with AI document intelligence, drafting, smart intake forms, and USCIS PDF autofill.

**Details:**
A fast-growing US immigration law firm, founded in Washington, doubled its footprint by acquiring an established immigration practice in Detroit. Overnight, the firm had two offices, two teams, two sets of habits — and one shared problem: the tooling. Case data lived in spreadsheets and a no-code database, exhibits were assembled by hand, and every off-the-shelf option they evaluated (Docketwise, Visalaw.ai, ManifestOS) forced them to bend their practice around someone else's workflow. Immigration law is document warfare. A single EB-5 petition can involve hundreds of source documents — bank statements, payslips, corporate records, affidavits — that must be classified, described, ordered into exhibit lists, and woven into a source-of-funds narrative that holds up to USCIS scrutiny. An H-1B premium processing case lives or dies by a 15-business-day federal clock. The firm needed: Lanos Logic designed and built a full multi-tenant, multi-office platform from the ground up — the kind of product the firm would otherwise license from a legal-tech vendor, except this one is shaped exactly around how they practice. The firm's previous stack ran on a no-code database with automation glue — fine at one office, breaking at two. We ran the new platform in parallel on staging, migrated case data into Postgres with backward-compatible record IDs, and kept every client-facing upload link functional. The Washington and Detroit teams switched over without a single lost case file. The firm now operates both offices on software that competes head-to-head with ManifestOS, Visalaw.ai, and Docketwise — except it is theirs. No per-seat licensing, no waiting on a vendor roadmap, and AI woven through the entire case lifecycle rather than bolted on. Attorneys draft from live case context, paralegals stopped assembling exhibits by hand, and clients answer one smart questionnaire instead of twelve PDF attachments.

URL: https://lanos-logic.com/case-studies/us-immigration-law-firm-ai-case-management-platform

### Twilio SMS + Notion Automation Student Pick-up

- Industry: Education · Vertical: Education · Type: Low-Code · Country: Hong Kong · Year: 2021
- Key results: 2,000+ Hours saved annually · 167 hrs Monthly hours saved · 3 days Delivered in

A Hong Kong school's SMS notification system connects teachers, students, and parents during student pick-up, saving over 2,000 hours a year of teacher, office-staff, and student learning time.

**Details:**
Develop a telephony-based notification system to streamline communication between parents, teachers, and students during the student pick-up process. The Hong Kong school required telephony application to be developed to notify individual teachers about parent arrival. The parent would dial the number from their phone. The solution was developed to integrate Twilio with internal student information system, which sent a Google Chat notification to the teachers upon parent arrival. The system would lookup parent phone number from the Student Information system, find the relevant class period, subject and teacher and send Google Chat notification to the relevant teacher. Conditions catered for multiple calls, so that only single notification would be sent, un-identified numbers, calling outside the given timeframe. Since student information system would not have external API the automated data import/export flow was developed to have data put into Notion. The third stakeholder in the process was the Business Office to monitor parent arrival live, so the Notion Dashboard was created to enable the stakeholder to monitor the process. To monitor Efficiency the solution Google Data Studio was plugged into the data collection. ## The ROI-First Method (Engagement Process)

Every engagement runs on the ROI-First Method — a three-phase approach (Analyze, Prepare, Implement) that targets your highest-return workflows first so each automation pays for itself before we move to the next.

1. **Analyze** — Plan, analyze, and blueprint business processes using BPMN and documentation.
2. **Prepare** — Refine and align processes with future state planning.
3. **Implement** — Deploy automations that deliver immediate results.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**General questions:**

Q: What AI automation services does Lanos Logic offer?
A: Lanos Logic offers AI Agents, Voice AI Agents, Vector Database Solutions, Document Automation, Process Automation, Social Media Automation, Communication Automation, Mobile App Development, and Analytics & Insights, plus enterprise cybersecurity delivered as always-on, AI-assisted systems rather than one-off audits, including white-label security packages for software agencies (application security testing — SAST, DAST, SCA, secret, container and IaC scanning — vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, and systems hardening with cloud posture management).

Q: How much does AI automation cost?
A: Every Lanos Logic solution is custom-scoped, so pricing depends on the workflows automated and the integrations required. We start with a free discovery call and a BPMN analysis, then quote a fixed project price before any build begins — no open-ended hourly billing.

Q: How long does an AI automation project take?
A: Most automation workflows are deployed within 2-6 weeks. Complex enterprise integrations may take 8-12 weeks. We follow a 3-phase process: Analyze, Prepare, and Implement.

Q: What results can businesses expect from AI automation?
A: Results vary by workflow, so we quote real ones rather than averages. The University of Minnesota saved 80% of its student-onboarding admin time. A law firm automated 10,000+ contracts and reclaimed 90 hours a month. A medical equipment testing company automated 9,600 certificates a year and redeployed 4 full-time staff. A voice AI deployment qualifies 100-150 leads a week at a 98% completion rate. Every figure we publish is attached to a named case study.

Q: Which industries does Lanos Logic serve?
A: We serve marketing and sales agencies, e-commerce, healthcare, real estate, logistics, education, professional services, manufacturing, government and public sector, pharmaceutical, life sciences, financial services, law firms and attorneys, and immigration law practices.
